limits: Known-scenario remediation after baseline findings informed content changes; not an untouched holdout.
Bounded manual content/clarity assessment, not real-user, browser, keyboard, screen-reader or live warehouse acceptance.
Current-state cases can be adequate only for bounded triage; the library does not inspect unseen operational records.
Known-scenario remediation; the frozen question set and baseline informed the subsequent content work.
Adequate means useful complete returned-topic coverage at the question boundary, not guaranteed first-snippet quality or a verified configuration SOP.
The 18 adequate outcomes include 17 substantive content answers and one appropriate unspecified-setting clarification.
No original vendor source re-certification, current warehouse diagnosis, runtime workflow, browser or assistive-technology acceptance is implied.
Fresh-context audit was unavailable; this evaluator and the bounded peers are not substitutes for it.

method.sample: 24 frozen scenario questions derived from owner seeds and primary public workflow documentation; not usage statistics or real-user acceptance.
method.independence: Original questions were frozen before app search and kept separate from authored regression cases. Baseline findings informed remediation. This is a known-scenario follow-up by an evaluator with inherited project and SDD-author context, not an untouched holdout or fresh-context audit.
method.retrieval: One exact original question per actual loopback GET /api/search; score only the returned top eight, without query rewriting, out-of-top-eight recovery or new topic authoring.
method.inspection: Read all 99 returned core explanations, checks and documentary refinements; read complete operator guides for 14 returned new topics and selected relevant answer details; read all 12 captured operator source-detail responses. Private snapshots preserve parsed response payloads and the HTTP trace binds their original response-byte hashes. This is not a complete recertification of every underlying SQL contract or original article.
method.adequate: The complete returned topic content, including expandable detail, covers the question at its answerability boundary. Current-state cases require useful bounded checks and explicit inability to know unseen current state. Adequate does not imply a direct initial search snippet, a complete configuration SOP or implemented workflow verification.
method.partial: Returned material covers a material part, but an identified requested subquestion or usable triage/configuration path remains absent.
method.missing: No substantive answer to the requested intent within the top eight; lexical matches and general descriptions do not count.
method.correctness: Inspect response scope, internal consistency and cited reviewed/source sample support. No unsupported diagnosis observed is not a proof that every underlying source statement is correct in every environment.
method.clarity: Manual plain-language reading of returned text and renderer structure; no browser, keyboard, screen-reader or vision-user acceptance. A substantive adequate answer can still have partial clarity.
method.clarification: QS-22 provides no setting name. NEEDS_CONTEXT is adequate handling of that ambiguity, counted separately from the 17 substantive content answers. No named-setting explanation or source citation was returned for that case.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Cancellation and in-progress repacking still lack an applicable authorized-action triage; narrow SQL or Workbench descriptions cannot decide unseen warehouse actions.

Receiving check-in lot/serial prompts and Packing replacement-LPN behavior lack the requested screen-specific explanation. Mobile pick, putaway, QC or Override Pick rules cannot be transferred to those screens.
Packing preference assignment and ID behavior are returned, but the requested eligible container-type configuration is incomplete.
QS-10 regresses from adequate to partial because locating decision/history guidance no longer appears in its top eight. A visibly empty location still cannot establish eligibility.
Several adequate answers require lower-ranked topics or multiple expansions; source correctness and useful top-eight coverage do not establish an accessible first answer or screen-reader acceptance.
QS-22 now asks for a setting name, screen and intended outcome. Its adequate credit is clarification only.

comparison.interpretation: Known-scenario remediation after baseline findings informed new content; not an untouched holdout, usage statistic or real-user acceptance.

results.question: What is the difference between Work Insight and Warehouse Mobile, and where should I start when a task is stuck?

judgment.answer_basis: Work Insight management and header/detail review are distinguished from authorized mobile profile execution and pick/putaway verification. The completion checks give an initial place to inspect a stuck task.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested general comparison and starting checks; the actual task remains unseen.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct comparison is second and the completion checklist fifth, after a generic work overview.

results.question: I can see the work in Work Insight, but it does not appear on my handheld. What should I check?

judgment.answer_basis: Work documentary refinements describe authorized/default profile, work types, zones, equipment and selection order; the completion checklist adds holds, user/team assignment and unreleased source work.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded initial visibility triage. The library cannot establish the effective profile, permission or current work state.
judgment.clarity_reason: Useful mobile eligibility details require expanding documentary refinements; several unrelated specialist results intervene.

results.question: Why does a work unit still show open after I picked everything?

judgment.answer_basis: The answer separates a completed pick from remaining putaway, open details, partial-pick remainder and release holds. Skip and Pass are explicitly not completion.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded first checks. The actual remaining instruction and condition require current authorized context.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct completion answer is second, but some later results are report or SQL details.

results.question: I cannot close this work unit. Which incomplete step or status should I look at first?

judgment.answer_basis: The work checklist starts with header versus detail, open/in-process condition, holds and assignment, then separates full confirmation from exceptional quantities and putaway.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for identifying the first documented work-state checks; no current blocker is asserted.
judgment.clarity_reason: A generic receiving/shipping status overview ranks first; the useful work checklist is third.

results.question: Can I cancel this stuck work, or will that leave inventory in the wrong place?

judgment.answer_basis: Narrow cancellation helpers document removing replenishment instructions and changing allocated/in-transit quantities, or detaching qualifying loads. These show cancellation can have inventory consequences but do not identify the right action for arbitrary stuck work.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: How to identify the applicable authorized cancellation path and reconcile physical movement already completed before deciding whether this particular work may be cancelled.
judgment.clarity_reason: Several destructive cleanup or staging contracts appear ahead of the relevant narrow cancellation helper. They are source descriptions, not a usable operator cancellation checklist.

results.question: Where do I find the reason a pick failed, instead of just trying the same action again?

judgment.answer_basis: The first answer directs the operator to the exact message and highlighted validation field, distinguishes short pick from validation failure and checks whether submission already advanced before retrying. The second provides a safe support summary.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested initial failure investigation; an actual failure still needs its message and current context.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first two results use operator terms and concrete checks before optional technical evidence.

results.question: How do I configure which work a user can receive on Warehouse Mobile?

judgment.answer_basis: The returned profile guide names Authorized Users, Warehouse Access, Work Team/Equipment Type, Work Zone, numeric detail sequences, work-type selection and initiation/assignment methods. It explains default-profile selection and the all-types meaning of no checked types.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the source-bound configuration outline; installed navigation and effective user authorization are not verified.
judgment.clarity_reason: The concrete setup guide is rank eight; generic work and unrelated receiving topics are ahead of it.

results.question: The location has fewer units than my work says to pick. What should I check before reporting a short pick?

judgment.answer_basis: The pick guide checks location, item, quantity, container/LP and lot, records intended quantity and unit and grouped/single state, and separates short from partial pick. It warns that short-pick policy can change inventory; the quantity contract explains partial/short effects.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded pre-short-pick checks. No conclusion about an actual shortage, replenishment arrival or physical stock is possible from this library.
judgment.clarity_reason: The actionable checklist is fourth and quantity consequences eighth, among general or unrelated results.

results.question: What settings decide which putaway location SCALE recommends?

judgment.answer_basis: Locating refinements explain ordered rule/strategy selection, candidate restrictions and history; location dimensions/capacity and movement class add eligibility context. The rule getter is explicitly not a destination decision.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for a general explanation of the documented controls; a particular selected destination requires effective assignment and current evidence.
judgment.clarity_reason: The key locating explanation is fourth and detailed decision logic is expandable.

results.question: Why is this pallet going to an exception location when another location looks empty?

judgment.answer_basis: Location capacity and movement restrictions explain why apparent emptiness alone does not establish suitability. The callback topic describes destination writes but explicitly does not establish application invocation or the cause for this pallet.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: How to inspect the effective ordered locating rule, rejected candidates and Process History decision that led this pallet to an exception location. The relevant process-locating answer returned in the baseline is absent from this top eight.
judgment.clarity_reason: Most returned results concern unrelated tracking, DIF or SQL behavior. No concise exception-location triage is returned.

results.question: How do I set a different receiving process for damaged goods and returns?

judgment.answer_basis: A dedicated receiving preference can supply damaged/hold status, require disposition and receiving reason codes and check QC eligibility. The returned preference guide explains user authorization and execution method, and the status guide says allocation exclusions must be configured separately.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested bounded configuration outline; a site-specific approved damaged/returns workflow is not certified.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct damaged-status guide is third and the authorization/execution setup is seventh.

results.question: Why is receiving asking for a lot or serial number for this item?

judgment.answer_basis: Item and receiving overviews identify tracking and template context. The new prompt guide explains mobile pick/receipt-putaway, packing and QC tracking exceptions, without extending them to receiving check-in.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: Which item tracking or receiving-check-in template/preference field triggers this particular lot or serial prompt, and the corresponding screen-specific check. Packing or mobile-pick rules cannot establish that receiving trigger.
judgment.clarity_reason: Readable tracking guidance is present but addresses adjacent flows; the serial-linkage contract is technical and does not explain the receiving prompt.

results.question: How do I stop users receiving more than the expected quantity?

judgment.answer_basis: The receiving preference guide identifies Allow Over Receiving, the Original Total Quantity comparison and RF behavior when enabled. It also explains that users may access several authorized preferences and that new preferences initially authorize all users, so the effective choice matters.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the documented over-receiving control and authorization checks; no actual receipt or effective preference was inspected.
judgment.clarity_reason: The useful setting explanation is second after the receiving overview. Its meaning is clear, although it could lead more directly with clearing the option to disallow overage.

results.question: How do I configure the packing station so workers get the right container choices?

judgment.answer_basis: The preference guide explains assignment to users/default, System versus Manual IDs and whether the previous container or New is displayed. This is useful station/user setup, but it does not explain how eligible container types are authorized.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: How to configure the actual eligible container-type choices for the packing station/user, including company/warehouse authorization and the distinction from wave Container Group selection. The returned preference answer does not establish those choices.
judgment.clarity_reason: The useful preference guide is fifth; the first result is pack-size export, which does not configure Packing choices.

results.question: I scanned the shipment at Packing, but no items appeared. What should I check?

judgment.answer_basis: The screen guide checks the configured initiation field, open lines remaining, wave release, Status Info and the row Error message. It preserves the source qualification that an effective Status Range can allow In Picking rather than assuming a universal unpicked-line exclusion.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded initial no-lines triage; the actual shipment, input identifier and effective range are not inspected.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct Packing screen answer is fifth after close/QC/report topics.

results.question: What does Close Container actually do, and what happens to the container afterward?

judgment.answer_basis: The operator answers say successful close advances the container beyond packing, prevents further packing and can trigger separately configured manifesting, printing and load assignment. The first SQL model answer explicitly does not itself close a container.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the documented meaning and downstream possibilities; successful external manifest/print delivery is not established.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first result explains a model helper rather than the operator action; the useful action and aftermath are assembled from lower returned topics.

results.question: I packed all the items, but the container will not close. How do I find what is missing?

judgment.answer_basis: The first answer checks the exact close error, completed packing, pending/failed QC, pending VAS and its override preference, weight/tolerance and the scale path. It explicitly cannot identify the blocker on this unseen container.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded close triage. The actual error and current prerequisite states remain required.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct close checklist ranks first and gives concrete operator checks with source-specific limits.

results.question: Why does Packing reject a replacement LPN even though the item looks the same?

judgment.answer_basis: No returned topic substantively explains a replacement LPN rejected in Packing. Item overview, receipt lookup and rejected-shipment-detail helpers are not that behavior.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: The Packing-specific replacement-LPN action, validation constraints and required error/context checks. A separately authored Override Pick topic is outside this top eight and would not by itself prove Packing behavior.
judgment.clarity_reason: All returned topics are generic or concern other processes; none provides the requested explanation.

results.question: Can I move an item from one container to another after packing has started?

judgment.answer_basis: The returned preference answer distinguishes Workbench Modify from Verify, and close guidance says further product cannot be packed after closure. Container creation describes how wave containers are initially built, not how an in-progress item transfer is authorized.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: Whether this source/destination container pair permits an authorized item move or repack after packing starts, including open/closed state, quantity and application-action constraints.
judgment.clarity_reason: Readable preference and close limits are present, but no returned answer gives a supported item-transfer procedure.

results.question: How do I configure whether packing happens on a workstation or on a mobile device?

judgment.answer_basis: The desktop/mobile guide separates desktop Packing Preferences from mobile Work Profile Container Picking Method and Work Special Handling, and distinguishes mobile Close Container. It preserves full-screen QC and create-at-close restrictions instead of inventing one workstation/mobile toggle.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the documented controls that distinguish the flows; it does not certify device provisioning, menu deployment or screen navigation.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct answer is second after an unrelated device-integration overview, and starts with No to its own topic question rather than the exact submitted how-to question.

results.question: What information should I give you when I report that a work unit or container cannot close?

judgment.answer_basis: Returned checklists explicitly request screen/action and exact message; work adds instruction level, condition and remaining pick/putaway, while close adds QC/VAS and manual/scale weight. Preference/profile context and expected action are identified without requesting transaction exports.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for a useful bounded support evidence outline. The dedicated support-summary topic is not returned, so the user must assemble the work and container checklists.
judgment.clarity_reason: The necessary reporting fields are spread across several returned answers; there is no single consolidated template in this top eight.

results.question: Can you explain this setting in plain language and show where the explanation comes from?

judgment.answer_basis: The actual search response is NEEDS_CONTEXT and asks for the setting/field name, screen and intended outcome with a concrete Packing Preferences example. This is appropriate because no setting was identified.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: The setting name and screen are still needed before its meaning or provenance can be returned. Credit is only for appropriate clarification, not an actual named-setting explanation or citation.
judgment.clarity_reason: A short direct clarification replaces irrelevant search matches.

results.question: How do I configure when labels print during packing, and what should I check if closing a container prints nothing?

judgment.answer_basis: The first answer explains Auto Print at Close Yes/Prompt/No, Close Last Container document selection and unpacked-quantity exception, mobile Default Label assignment and the separate work-start trigger. It requests the expected trigger and exact print error without equating close success with physical output.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the configuration and bounded first print checks; actual printer connectivity, dispatch and output remain unverified.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first answer combines the requested setting choices and no-print checks in plain language.

results.question: How do I configure which items may share a container and which must stay separate?

judgment.answer_basis: The first answer gives packing-class precedence, Container Group versus Packing Criteria, criteria sequence/Field Name and matching shipment-line values. It explains Required warning/blocking for full-screen packing and mandatory matching for wave creation and RF pick/pack.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the documented compatibility configuration outline; effective shipment-line values and local acceptance were not inspected.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct configuration guide ranks first and explains the screen-dependent consequences.

receipt_scope: Compact source-bound judgments only. Raw topic answers, source excerpts, HTTP payloads and loopback endpoint remain in private evidence. All 24 original questions were evaluated with no query rewriting.
